Subject: Recap + next steps (VPC option)

Hi Tom / Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — good to learn more about Acme's roadmap for the personalization engine and the latency targets you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary workload: real-time personalization for web + mobile (max 150 req/s, 50K tokens/day)
- Latency SLO: 150–200ms 95th p50 for text gen paths
- Data concerns: PII in prompts, customer wants VPC/on-prem options for model+data isolation
- Timeline: evaluating solutions this quarter, procurement expected in Q2 if pilot goes well

Proposed next steps:
1) Share Redwood Dedicated / Private one-pager (attached) — gives sizing/pricing bands for dedicated GPU pools and VPC options.
2) Schedule a short technical sync with Dylan to validate network/ingress requirements (30 min).
3) If VPC/private is appealing, we can assemble a checklist for a proof-of-concept (SLA, data path, KMS integration, compliance docs).

Can you confirm which of the following is highest priority: (A) POC with hosted API to prove latency/cost, (B) Proof-of-concept on Dedicated in your VPC, or (C) Internal procurement review first? Knowing that will help me align next outreach.

I attached the Redwood_Dedicated_Overview.pdf and my post-call notes.

Availability: I can do the technical sync with Dylan on Mon/Tue (9:30–11am PT). If that works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —

Quick hit on sizing / procurement items (high-level):
- Rough sizing: 1–2 A100-equivalent GPUs for pilot (depending on model choice / quantization). For 150 req/s steady-state you’ll likely need an elastic pool (min 1, max 3) to meet 95th p latency with bursts.
- We’ll include two price bands in the SOW: pilot (30-day) pricing and committed reserved pricing (monthly).
- Procurement docs we plan to attach: standard SOW template, SOC 2 attestation, terms summary.

I attached the dedicated overview again; I’ll follow up after the tech sync with a draft SOW and procurement-ready quote.

One quick check: Where does this sit in your procurement timeline now? If timelines shifted, let me know — we can prioritize the SOW vs. a faster pilot on hosted to validate performance without procurement friction.

Cheers,
Marissa
